plans.rationale: This is the first round. We need to establish the exact symptom onset and check error rates and connection pool metrics for the symptomatic services payments-api and ledger-service, as well as investigate all recent changes and the dependency map around these services.

tasks.goal: Check logs and error metrics for connection pool exhaustion and database errors to establish the exact onset time and scale of failures for payments-api and ledger-service.
Review all recent configuration changes, deploys, feature flags, and infrastructure modifications across all services, and inspect the dependency graph around payments-api and ledger-service.
Check logs and error metrics for connection pool exhaustion and database errors to establish the exact onset time and scale of failures for payments-api and ledger-service.
Review all recent configuration changes, deploys, feature flags, and infrastructure modifications across all services, and inspect the dependency graph around payments-api and ledger-service.
Build and rank competing root-cause hypotheses

r1-observability-1.summary: At 13:14 to 13:15 UTC, ledger-service experienced database connection pool exhaustion (HikariPool-1 total=5, active=5, waiting up to 835), causing p99 latency to spike to over 7200ms and error rates to jump to ~10%. This triggered upstream 503 errors and connection failures in payments-api starting at 13:15 UTC, driving payments-api error rates up to ~8%.

findings.statement: ledger-service latency_p99_ms began rising at 2026-10-06T13:14:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 7278.17ms at 13:41:00+00:00.
ledger-service error_rate_pct started its anomalous increase at 2026-10-06T13:15:00+00:00, peaking at 10.25%.
payments-api error_rate_pct started its anomalous increase at 2026-10-06T13:15:00+00:00, peaking at 8.26%.
ledger-service first logged HikariPool-1 connection timeout errors at 2026-10-06T13:15:05+00:00 indicating connection pool exhaustion (total=5, active=5, idle=0).
payments-api first logged downstream connection acquisition failures when calling ledger-service at 2026-10-06T13:15:02+00:00.

open_questions: What caused the spike in waiting database requests on ledger-service to exhaust the pool size of 5?

r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped service dependencies around payments-api and ledger-service and reviewed changes across all services for the past 7 days, identifying a configuration change that reduced ledger-service database pool max size right before the incident.

findings.statement: payments-api makes synchronous calls to ledger-service, upi-gateway, fraud-service, and redis-cache, and asynchronous calls to event-bus.
ledger-service makes synchronous calls to ledger-db.
A configuration change chg-8919 occurred on ledger-service at 2026-10-06T13:12:00+00:00, normalizing db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5.
Routine deployment chg-8200 on event-bus and chg-8270 on fraud-service occurred shortly before the incident on 2026-10-06.
The reduction of db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 in ledger-service right before ~13:15 is temporally aligned with the start of DB connection errors.

open_questions: Whether the reduced connection pool size of 5 for ledger-service was sufficient for peak traffic load.

hypotheses.title: Database connection pool size reduction in ledger-service
hypotheses.mechanism: A configuration change normalized ledger-service database pool max size from 50 to 5, immediately causing connection pool exhaustion under normal traffic loads and leading to timeouts and errors in payments-api.

supporting.note: Config change reduced ledger-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 right before onset
Latency began rising sharply starting at 13:14 UTC
Error rate surged starting at 13:15 UTC
Ledger-service logged HikariPool-1 connection timeout errors with active=5 and high waiting requests
Payments-api logged downstream connection acquisition failures when calling ledger-service

hypotheses.title: Routine deployment regression in event-bus
hypotheses.mechanism: Routine deployment on event-bus introduced an unhandled error or resource leak that subsequently affected downstream services.

supporting.note: Routine deploy chg-8200 occurred on event-bus shortly before the incident

contradicting.note: Directly links the connection pool exhaustion to ledger-service configuration change rather than event-bus
Logs specifically point to ledger-service database connection pool exhaustion rather than event-bus failures

assumptions: The event-bus deployment caused an indirect cascading failure resulting in database connection exhaustion on ledger-service.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The onset of the incident is established at 13:14 UTC when ledger-service latency began to rise, followed immediately by error rate spikes and connection pool exhaustion at 13:15 UTC. The root cause is unequivocally linked to configuration change chg-8919, which reduced the database pool max size to 5 just minutes before the onset. Alternative hypotheses like event-bus deployments lack direct evidence and causal alignment.

adjustments.reason: Directly supported by configuration change chg-8919 reducing pool max size from 50 to 5 right before onset, backed by connection timeout logs and metric anomalies.
Contradicted by direct log and configuration evidence pointing to ledger-service database pool exhaustion.
